subject: paediatrics
title: Neuromuscular and developmental disorders: DMD, SMA and cerebral palsy

steps.tx: The panels show **Duchenne muscular dystrophy**, an X linked dystrophin disorder, through Gowers sign, enlarged calves, absent dystrophin and later wheelchair use. The boy climbs up his own legs to stand, creatine kinase rises into the thousands, and steroids prolong walking by years. **Becker dystrophy** is milder with an in frame deletion, while myotonic dystrophy adds grip myotonia with cataracts. Heart and spine surveillance matters because **cardiomyopathy** and scoliosis progress silently over time.
steps.say: Duchenne dystrophy makes the boy climb up his legs because hip muscles have weakened greatly. Calves look enlarged and creatine kinase rises into the thousands in blood tests. Steroids prolong walking and clinicians monitor the heart and spine throughout childhood carefully. Becker disease follows a milder course and myotonic disease adds delayed grip release.

vis.alt: A four-panel image showing a child with Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy demonstrating Gowers' sign, enlarged calves, absent dystrophin on muscle biopsy, and a child in a wheelchair.
vis.caption: DMD: Gowers' sign, calf pseudohypertrophy, absent dystrophin, and wheelchair use

steps.tx: **Spinal muscular atrophy** deletes SMN1 and leaves a floppy infant with frog leg posture, tongue fasciculations and weak cry from motor neuron loss. Type 1 disease never achieves sitting, while newborn screening now lets treatment start before symptoms destroy neurons. **Nusinersen** given intrathecally, one time gene therapy and oral risdiplam all raise SMN protein by different routes. Botulism, myasthenia and Guillain Barre syndrome mimic floppiness, and cough support with night ventilation protects breathing.
steps.say: Spinal muscular atrophy is caused by deletion of a survival motor neuron gene and the infant is floppy at rest. Tongue fasciculations appear and type one disease never achieves independent sitting without treatment. Newborn screening finds babies early and gene based treatments raise the missing protein. Cough assistance and night ventilation protect breathing when muscles weaken further.

steps.tx: The illustration links a **frog leg floppy infant** with a motor neuron that has lost SMN1, the gene deletion behind spinal muscular atrophy type 1. Inside the neuron, **nusinersen** alters SMN2 splicing to include exon 7, while AAV9 delivers a working SMN1 copy once intravenously. That contrast teaches why early treatment rescues neurons before they die. For the exam, you should connect newborn screening with presymptomatic therapy and better sitting outcomes.
steps.say: The picture shows a floppy infant below and a motor neuron without working SMN1 above. Nusinersen changes SMN2 splicing and AAV9 delivers a replacement gene once intravenously. Each treatment helps raise SMN protein and early use helps rescue neurons before death occurs. Newborn screening matters because presymptomatic treatment gives the best motor outcomes.

vis.caption: Floppy infant with SMN neuron gene and splicing therapies. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Cerebral palsy** follows early brain injury and presents as spastic diplegia with scissoring after prematurity, hemiplegia after stroke, or dyskinetic movements after kernicterus. Imaging often shows periventricular leukomalacia, and treatment combines physiotherapy, baclofen for generalised spasticity and botulinum toxin for focal tightness. **Neural tube defects** need folate prevention, with 4 mg daily for high risk mothers, and myelomeningocele adds shunt and latex allergy issues. Developmental red flags include lost milestones at any age.
steps.say: Cerebral palsy follows early brain injury and spastic diplegia causes scissoring of the legs. Prematurity injures periventricular white matter and physiotherapy keeps joints moving throughout childhood daily. Baclofen eases generalised tightness and botulinum toxin relaxes selected focal muscles well. Lost milestones always worry clinicians because development should never go backwards.

steps.tx: **Guillain Barre syndrome** climbs from the legs with lost reflexes and may need immunoglobulin or plasma exchange when weakness threatens breathing or walking. Charcot Marie Tooth disease gives pes cavus with distal wasting, and myasthenia gives fatigable weakness that pyridostigmine improves. **Autism and ADHD** also feature in this lesson, with joint attention, stimulant treatment and school support plans shaping daily function. The table below contrasts dystrophy, motor neuron disease, cerebral palsy and peripheral neuropathy for revision.
steps.say: Guillain Barre syndrome is an ascending weakness and reflexes are lost as weakness develops upward from the legs. Immunoglobulin or plasma exchange helps severe cases and breathing needs close monitoring daily. Myasthenia weakens muscles with use and rest restores strength for a while. School plans coordinate therapy and learning support for every affected child.
